title: Optimization with Non-Differentiable Constraints with Applications to Fairness, Recall, Churn, and Other Goals
authors: Andrew Cotter, Heinrich Jiang, Maya Gupta, Serena Wang, Taman Narayan, Seungil You, Karthik Sridharan
conclusions: Introduces the 'proxy-Lagrangian' formulation for training non-convex models (e.g. neural nets) subject to non-convex and/or non-differentiable 'rate constraints' (linear combinations of positive/negative classification rates over datasets), where the standard Lagrangian's pure Nash equilibrium may not exist and cannot be optimized with gradients.

Reformulates training as a two-player non-zero-sum game whose solution concept ('semi-coarse correlated equilibrium') provably yields an approximately feasible and optimal stochastic classifier, extending prior zero-sum-game work (Agarwal et al. 2018) to the non-differentiable, non-convex setting.

Gives a 'shrinking' procedure that reduces a T-iterate stochastic solution down to a sparse mixture of at most m+1 deterministic models (m = number of constraints), with theoretical guarantees, plus a practical SGD-based algorithm and open-source TF library.

Surveys and formalizes a broad taxonomy of rate constraints -- coverage, recall/precision/AUC, churn/win-loss-ratio, and group fairness goals (statistical parity, equal opportunity/odds, minimum coverage, no-lost-benefits, etc.) -- all expressed as expectations/rates over a distribution (inductive setting), not as hard per-instance counts on a fixed test set.

Demonstrates the approach experimentally across benchmark and real-world datasets on a range of these rate-constraint goals; the mechanism (proxy-Lagrangian, multiplier ascent as a projected-gradient regret player) is squarely a constrained-training / dual-ascent-style method, distinct from post-hoc adjustment.
our_use: main.tex lines 178-187 (paragraph 'Rate-constrained learning'): 'non-differentiable rate constraints through proxy-Lagrangian games \citep{cotter2019optimization} ... These bound expected rates over a distribution, inductively. Our requirement is a hard count on one specific test set: transductive, verified on the argmax predictions themselves, and paired with per-group local caps.'
issues: none -- author list, title, journal, volume (20), article number (172), pages (1-59), and year (2019) all verified against the PDF front matter and cross-checked against the JMLR listing (jmlr.org/papers/v20/18-616.html). The citing sentence's characterization ('non-differentiable rate constraints through proxy-Lagrangian games') is an accurate one-clause summary of the paper's central contribution (Sections 1.4-1.6, 4), and the follow-on distinction ('bound expected rates over a distribution, inductively' vs. our transductive hard count on one fixed test set with per-group local caps) is factually correct: Cotter et al.'s rate constraints (Eq. 6-8, Table 1-3) are defined as proportions p+/p- over arbitrary (training or auxiliary) datasets under an inductive/expectation guarantee (Theorem 2 bounds E[g_i] over a distribution), not as hard argmax-verified counts on a designated transductive test set.
